rules.body: Apply this guidance when deferred persistent work outlives the current observer and consumption can synchronously reenter navigation. Evidence: README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription."

Route edits into the existing document buffer's trailing task. Each edit restarts its 120 ms quiet interval; consume only the latest text, and leave the task reusable after consumption. Evidence: TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." src/coordinator.js: "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))".

Keep document buffers owned by BufferBank and keyed by document identity. Retiring a badge must clean up its subscription without discarding pending document text. On open, close, and dispose, synchronously flush the departing buffer before the operation returns, preserving persistence that immediate writes previously provided. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Original src/coordinator.js: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}" and "dispose(){api.close();}".

Before flushing a departing buffer, detach the old view and complete its subscription cleanup and clearing render. Avoid stale view mutations after flushing, because saving may synchronously select a newer view. After retirement returns, an outer open must check that its request is still current before publishing its destination. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." Original src/coordinator.js: "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;" and "const old=getView();setView(null);".

Clear the consumed task's pending timer and value before invoking its consumer, so a synchronous callback cannot consume the same pending edit again and later pushes remain usable. Retain the existing utility's behavior rather than making saving a terminal task state. Evidence: src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Preserve public methods, document identities, original text including empty strings, document-specific status filtering, and payload meanings. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()." and "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." src/coordinator.js: "if(event.id===id)env.renderStatus(event);".

Keep the adjacent preview's separate 40 ms trailing task and cancel-on-hide policy. Do not apply document persistence policy to transient preview work. Evidence: TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));\n  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Verify with controlled timers that edits produce no write before 120 ms of quiet, write the latest text once at that boundary, and save a subsequent burst independently. Check pending edits on open, close, and dispose, including empty text and reopening the same document. Use synchronous save listeners that open another document or close; assert that the callback's selection and rendering remain authoritative after the outer operation returns. Check subscription cleanup and unchanged preview timing, hide cancellation, and reuse. These checks derive from TASK: "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and docs/host-api.md: "Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled."

limitations: Applies to persistent document work with a separate view subscription and synchronous save callbacks; transient work may require a different departure policy.
The public task and sources do not specify exception recovery, input validation, or behavior for non-text values.
Attempt 1 supplies one successful implementation example; its reported results do not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit across other tasks.
The AST hint and automatic contracts are review aids, not independent requirements.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
